title: Crown and Wolf
premise: Sable Kavanagh has spent her life as a royal food-taster in the Vale of Ashenmoor, a valley where magic cannot enter, poisoning herself in small doses to build immunity for a king she's never met. When a mute child arrives speaking the dead tongue of Vhalen—a kingdom erased from every map and memory—Sable discovers she is the last living heir to that vanished throne, and the child is her realm's final spell made flesh. Hunted by the king's sorcerers who fear what her inheritance could unmake, Sable must find the Door of Thirteenth Moons, the only way into a country that no longer exists, before the moon completes its thirteenth turn and the child—and Vhalen's last magic—dies forever. In the end, Sable chooses to open the door not to reclaim a crown but to release the trapped kingdom, sacrificing her claim and her immunity-gained safety to give Vhalen a true death and the child a living name.
about_author: Ivo Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, linguistic, and moral—from a farmhouse full of unlabeled maps.

chapters.title: The Taster's Table
chapters.summary: POV Sable. We meet Sable mid-meal, swallowing a suspect broth meant for King Aldric's envoy, and feel the numb discipline of her craft: poison as routine, the vale's magic-dead silence as comfort. A letter arrives summoning her to the capital. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced calm—the first crack in a life built on small controlled harms.

chapters.title: A Knock at Frostfall
chapters.summary: POV Sable. On her last night in the valley, a barefoot child appears at her door during a snowstorm, speaking a language no one alive should know. The words make Sable's old scars ache and the fire burn green. She realizes with horror that magic—which cannot exist here—is standing in her kitchen. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear; the safe world ends tonight.

chapters.title: The Word That Unmade a Kingdom
chapters.summary: POV Sable. A dying linguist-priest, Mother Ilsen, recognizes the child's speech as High Vhalenic and names it: the tongue of a kingdom struck from history two centuries ago. The child speaks one word at Sable—her true name, Kavanagh of Vhalen—and Ilsen dies smiling. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited identity; Sable learns she was never ordinary, only hidden.

chapters.title: Roads Out of the Vale
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Fleeing before the king's riders arrive, Sable takes the child—whom she names Wren—and crosses the vale's boundary for the first time. Magic floods back into the world like sound after deafness, overwhelming and beautiful. Wren stops speaking entirely outside the vale. Emotional beat: grief and awe entwined; freedom feels like drowning.

chapters.title: The Gilded Cage of Aldric's Court
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Instead of running far, Sable gambles on hiding inside the capital itself, resuming her taster post under a false name. She observes King Aldric up close: charming, exhausted, and terrified of something he won't name. His sorcerer, Lord Corvane, watches her too closely. Emotional beat: tension of proximity; the hunter's house becomes her shelter.

chapters.title: What the King Is Afraid Of
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. In his chambers, Aldric confesses to a portrait of his father: every heir of his line has dreamed of a door, and each died within a year of coronation. He believes Vhalen was erased for good reason and that anything returning from it must be destroyed. Emotional beat: sympathetic antagonist established; fear dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Corvane catches Sable translating a Vhalenic glyph and, instead of exposing her, offers protection—for a price: bring him the child. He shows her a cell where 'returned things' are kept, things that came through before and were never human again. Emotional beat: temptation and revulsion; kindness as a hook.

chapters.title: Wren's Nightsong
chapters.summary: POV Wren (rendered impressionistically). The child dreams in the erased kingdom: towers of glass, a queen with Sable's face, a door of moonlight closing. Each dream, Wren wakes weaker, fading like ink in water. Emotional beat: tender melancholy; we understand Wren is not a messenger but a message running out of time.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Following Ilsen's notes, Sable finds Osk, a disgraced cartographer imprisoned for mapping places that don't exist. He agrees to help find the Door of Thirteenth Moons if she'll admit, out loud, that his maps were true. Emotional beat: wry alliance; two people restored by being believed.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Osk explains the mechanics: the door opens only when the moon completes a thirteenth turn—an impossible lunar month that begins now and ends at winter solstice. Wren will not survive past it. The countdown structure locks in. Emotional beat: dread converted into purpose; a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Poison and Proof
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At a state banquet, Sable tastes a dish laced with something worse than toxin—it carries a compulsion charm aimed at the king. Her trained immunity lets her resist long enough to expose the plot, saving Aldric's life. Corvane knows she could only do this because of Vhalen blood. Emotional beat: competence and peril; her curse becomes her shield, briefly.

chapters.title: The Debt of a Saved King
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. Owed a boon by law, Sable asks not for gold but for access to the royal archive's sealed Vhalen vault. Aldric grants it against Corvane's counsel, torn between gratitude and terror. Emotional beat: fragile trust between enemies; mercy as risk.

chapters.title: The Vault of Erasure
chapters.summary: POV Sable. In the vault, Sable finds her family's history: Kavanaghs were Vhalen's tasters too, sworn to die for their queen—and her grandmother smuggled the last spell-child out when the kingdom chose self-erasure over conquest. The erasure was Vhalen's own act, a wound they inflicted on themselves. Emotional beat: devastating inheritance; her lineage is love expressed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Moonrise
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Corvane seizes Wren, revealing he engineered the banquet poison to bind Sable to him—he wants the door opened so he can take Vhalen's power for himself. Sable barely escapes with Osk's help, leaving her court protections burning behind her. Emotional beat: betrayal and flight; the cost of every alliance comes due.

chapters.title: Hunted Across the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: POV Sable and Osk alternating. A brutal overland chase toward the coast where the door stands. Wren grows translucent; Sable feeds the child her own blood-earned resilience through an old Vhalenic rite, weakening herself. Emotional beat: fierce tenderness under exhaustion; love as literal expenditure of self.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sheltering in a chapel half-swallowed by the sea, Sable and Aldric—who has pursued them alone, without Corvane—finally speak honestly. He admits the kings' deaths were Vhalen calling its tasters home, and that he fears the door more than he fears Corvane. Emotional beat: enemy-to-ally turn; shared fear dissolves duty's armor.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV multiple. At the Door of Thirteenth Moons, Corvane arrives with soldiers and forces the threshold early, tearing it half-open. Raw Vhalen spills out: ghosts, memories, the screaming beauty of a dead nation. Osk holds the map-line steady at the cost of his sight. Emotional beat: chaos and awe; the impossible made violently real.

chapters.title: The Queen in the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Inside the half-open door, Sable meets the echo of Queen Maren—her ancestor—who offers her the crown and the power to restore Vhalen whole, at the price of becoming its eternal keeper, as all Kavanagh tasters were meant to be. Emotional beat: the central choice crystallized; power offered in the shape of love.

chapters.title: Crown and Wolf
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Climax. Corvane crosses the threshold to seize the crown; the wolf-shaped guardian of Vhalen's gate mauls the boundary between worlds. Sable refuses the crown, instead taking the taster's oath inverted: she will swallow Vhalen's ending herself, tasting the kingdom's death so Wren needn't carry it. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; duty transformed rather than obeyed.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV Sable. As the moon completes its impossible turn, Sable drinks the kingdom's last light. Vhalen closes—not erased this time, but finished, mourned, laid to rest. Corvane, emptied of his prize, is taken by the guardian. Wren solidifies into a real, mortal child with a real name: Lark. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into peace; the door shuts gently.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Aldric offers Sable a place at court—honored, protected, perhaps loved—but she declines the gilded role. She and Osk, half-blind, and little Lark return to the vale, where magic still cannot follow, and that absence finally feels like mercy rather than exile. Emotional beat: bittersweet homecoming; choosing smallness freely.

chapters.title: The Last Dish
chapters.summary: POV Sable, epilogue. Years later, Sable cooks a meal with no one to taste it for danger—just family at the table. Lark speaks Vhalenic as a mother tongue of memory, singing it like a lullaby. On the solstice, far away, a door-shaped shadow in the snow does not open, and Sable smiles. Emotional beat: resolution; love outlasting kingdoms, duty fulfilled by letting go.
